Officer's narrative
Driver 1 was traveling southbound on a multi-lane arterial in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle ahead slowed for
traffic. Drievr 2 was following Driver 1 and did not stop in time, striking the rear of Driver 1's vehicle with considerable
force. A Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle at the time of impact. Officers on
scene interviewed both drivers and the Passenger, and independent witnesses who stopped at the lcoation gave
statements consistent with what the drivers described. Driver 2 acknowledged following too closely and did not
dispute the sequence of events. Photographs taken at the scene show the rear damage to Driver 1's vehicle and the
position of both vehicles after impact. Driver 1 reported being dazed immediately after the collision and was later
evaluated by medical staff for a suspected concussion, a finding that fits the nature and force of this type of impact.
Officers noted that Driver 1's vehicle had no visible earlier damage, and Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the
policy covering the vehicle. Some of the damage observed to the vehicle's interior and undercarriage may not have
resulted from this collision alone, and the extent to which it did cannot be determined from the scene evidence.
